original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

actual_scope: #1166 OPEN ENDS item 5b (DreamingOfClouds): test the B-independent first-order jet certificate (#2162 Corollary J) on the #2111 121-line T=3 unit-world pool (certificate 119 against v=121): exact rigidity of (J1), Lemma F flows, inclusion-minimal immovable unit atoms with CR2 status and exact minimum cost, and a time-boxed search for a large jet-certifiable sub-pool.
scope_change_reason: The generic complex-rank-shape-decoder card is crowded; its decoder sub-line contains the live T=3 copied-information floor question (A) (cost >= v), whose open interval cost(pool) in [119, 121] (#2111) was posted as a test for new lower-bound techniques. This package applies one such technique (Corollary J) to that object and records exactly where and why it fails; no supplier, word or kappa is touched.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the three-total decoder line: (A) at T=3 decides whether three-total decoders can beat copied-information floor v. The result shows the first-order char-2 jet method cannot close the 119..121 gap on the pool and supplies small exact test atoms for any replacement method. No direct effect on the selected kappa.
stop_rule: Stop searching at 2026-10-15T05:58:35Z; ship the Q1+Q2 rigidity certificate plus fully checked Q3 atoms; Q4 is a failed search (no larger certifiable sub-pool found), not a bound; jet failure is not evidence against (A); any cost < v atom would need two independent rank computations (none found: Python and C enumerations agree; all costs >= v, with 4 tight 5-line orbits at cost = v).
evidence: verify.py (stdlib, ~60 s; --full adds ~8 min): (J1) on the pool has 2646 rows, 510 unknowns, F2 rank 266 (two implementations); the 245 explicit gauge/torus motions span the 244-dim solution space; delta'_t vanishes on it for all 30 harmonic lines (Corollary J fails for every homomorphism phi into every char-2 field); 30 explicit Lemma F flows (10-14 edges, even); exhaustive: no immovable sub-configuration with <= 3 lines, and the immovable 4-line ones form one orbit (12 members, cost 5 = v+1, not CR2); exhaustive: the inclusion-minimal immovable 5-line sub-configurations form 353 orbits, none CR2 over GF(2..16), exact cost - v distribution {0:4,1:103,2:184,3:55,4:7}, so (A) holds on all of them and 4 orbits are tight (cost = v) with neither jet nor CR2 certificate; 42 orbits of inclusion-minimal immovable atoms (v=4..10, 8-17 free incidences), none CR2 over GF(2),GF(4),GF(8),GF(16), exact minimum cost v+1..v+5 (C enumall and independent Python agree); B-dependent jet passes on all 1305 atom minimisers; the pool and 17 atoms are rigid modulo gauge+torus, so the uniform order-m jet fails at every order (Proposition R, proved in README); the #2162 order-2 test fails on all 42 atoms; best certifiable sub-pool found 103 lines (cost(pool) >= 103 < Theorem U 106 < MCC 119). tied_min control is movable; corrupted flow/incidence/pool/phi, atom-deletion and order-2 controls are rejected.

open_questions.question: Which certificate proves cost >= v directly on the strongly connected minimal immovable atoms (the 4-line orbit, 111 strongly connected 5-line orbits, 3 of 42 stored atoms)? The 4 tight 5-line orbits are already certified by #2111 Lemma SCC/Peel plus Corollary J on components.
open_questions.why_it_matters: They are the smallest unit-world cases not reduced by SCC/Peel, first-order jets or CR2 over GF(2^k), k <= 4; all have slack >= 1.
open_questions.first_step: Add an SCC/Peel classification to verify.py, then run CR2 over GF(32)/GF(64) and the #2162 section-3 split bound (under audit in #2330) on them.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing; not run in this session.

open_questions.question: Do jets around other characteristic-2 base points (not the phi-collapse, e.g. GF(4) partial realisations with a different vanishing diagonal set) certify the pool or its atoms?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The rigidity proved here is specific to the base point phi(P); Corollary J does not use other degenerations.
open_questions.first_step: For the 4-line atom, enumerate support-compatible incidence-preserving GF(4) base points and run the (J1)/(J2) test around each.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs a stated valued-realisation lemma for non-phi base points (VCR2 covers it, but the order bookkeeping must be redone).

open_questions.question: What is the largest Corollary-J-certifiable sub-pool S (search found 103 = pool minus the 18 lines through two points)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: cost(pool) >= |S|; reaching 106 would match Theorem U by an independent route, though not MCC 119.
open_questions.first_step: Exact search over unions of point-classes (lines grouped by p) using the order-48 symmetry, then local search with 2-for-1 swaps.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only greedy and 1-out/2-in swaps were tried; no upper bound on certifiable |S| is known beyond 120.

open_questions.question: Do order >= 3 jets, or non-uniform VCR2 realisations around the phi-collapse, certify any of the 25 non-rigid atoms?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Order 2 fails on all atoms and the 17 rigid atoms fail at every uniform order (Proposition R); the non-rigid atoms are the only place the jet route at the collapse is still open.
open_questions.first_step: Extend lib/order2.py to order 3 on the smallest non-rigid atom.
open_questions.blocked_by: The order-3 system is quadratic in the order-1 jet; needs a Groebner-free formulation.
